intro.title: Multi-Tab Auth Sync
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a React application that keeps a user's login status synchronized across multiple browser tabs. You will learn to use the Broadcast Channel API to send messages between tabs, ensuring that logging in or out in one tab automatically updates the auth state in all others. The core programming concept is managing shared state across different instances of the same application using browser-native communication. You'll work with React state, event handlers, and TypeScript to create a secure and responsive multi-tab experience. By the end, you'll understand how to implement real-time auth synchronization for a seamless user experience.
intro.usecase: Multi-tab auth sync is essential for modern web applications where users frequently work across multiple browser tabs. In banking dashboards, financial data must remain secure and consistent across all open tabs—logging out in one tab should immediately revoke access in others. E-commerce platforms use this pattern to prevent users from accidentally making purchases with expired sessions in background tabs. Enterprise applications like project management tools (Jira, Asana) synchronize authentication state to ensure team members don't work with stale credentials when switching between tabs. This pattern provides security and seamless user experience by maintaining consistent session state across the entire browsing context.
